summary: This note describes the 2016 World Series, the championship series of Major League Baseball's 2016 season and the 112th edition of the series. It was a best-of-seven playoff between the National League champion Chicago Cubs and the American League champion Cleveland Indians, the first postseason meeting of those franchises. The Indians had home-field advantage because the AL won the 2016 All-Star Game, which was the last World Series to use that rule. The note's two passages give different end dates for the series (November 3 and November 2).
one_line: Overview of the 2016 World Series, the MLB championship between the Chicago Cubs and Cleveland Indians, the first postseason meeting of those franchises.
key_facts: The 2016 World Series was the championship series of Major League Baseball's (MLB) 2016 season.
It was the 112th edition of the World Series.
It was a best-of-seven playoff between the National League (NL) champion Chicago Cubs and the American League (AL) champion Cleveland Indians.
The 2016 World Series was the first meeting of the Chicago Cubs and Cleveland Indians in postseason history.
The series was played between October 25 and November 3, according to the first passage of the note.
The second passage of the note gives the series end date as November 2 instead of November 3.
The Indians had home-field advantage because the American League had won the 2016 All-Star Game.
The 2016 World Series was the last World Series to have home-field advantage determined by All-Star Game results.
Since 2017, home-field advantage in the World Series is awarded to the team with the better record.
